newsitem.title: UK: Consumer coffee stocks fall in Feb yr/yr -- ED&F Man.
newsitem.headline: Consumer coffee stocks fall in Feb yr/yr -- ED&F Man.

text.p: World consumer coffee stocks stood at 8.3 million bags in February, up from 7.8 million in January but 300,000 bags lower than in February 1996, UK trade house E D & F Man said on Monday.
February stocks remained low and were equivalent to just six weeks of importing country demand, Man said.

But it said stock situation is expected to ease as Central American coffee continues to arrive while roastings fall moving into the western hemisphere spring and the implementation of retail price increases.
Man said the February data showed that the large shipments from origin seen since the start of the coffee year were at last starting to feed through into green coffee increase.
Roaster offtake was reported to be extremely high ahead of the Easter break.
Man said it adjusted the so-called European "non-reported" stock figures to reflected warehouse statistics obtained from the two ports of Genoa in Italy and Koper in Slovenia.
All stock figures for the last year had been altered to take account of the new figures.
"The net effect of this adjustment is to increase stock levels by some 200,000 bags, although stock changes remain more or less consistent," Man said.

Total stocks in the U.S. rose slightly by 204,000 to 1.54 million bags in February. Houston and Laredo stocks together accounted for 172,000 bags of this increase reflecting large shipments from Mexico.
Mexican shipments in the first five months of the 1996/97 crop year were some 340,000 bags above their level the previous year, although some of this is now finding its way into European stocks.
European stocks rose by 200,000 bags to 5.5 million bags in Febuary from January while stocks in Japan reached 1.12 million against 1.07 million in January.

Coffee had rallied strongly since the start of the year with the recently-expired March arabica in New York hitting a peak of 219.76 cents a lb on March 5 from over $1.00 at the start of 1997. The rally has since stalled.
Man said "The rise has been unique, because the coffee price has never been moved so far, or so fast, without a disaster in Brazil." --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
